Opal once debugged a firmware bug in a live ad-hoc sensor network during a server outage. She rerouted data through a custom RTOS layer, keeping 98% of edge nodes operational for 4 hours until a permanent fix. Her calm under pressure and knack for reverse-engineering binary logs saved our campaign from a $20k revenue drop.  

Opal is a self-taught firmware wizard who treats hardware as an extension of code. She built a Python-based tool to automate sensor calibration, cutting setup time by 40%. While her C/C++ expertise is legendary, what stands out is her obsession with aligning hardware constraints with software efficiency—like optimizing a legacy IoT protocol stack to meet 5ms latency targets.  

Her strength lies in turning ambiguous specs into reliable systems. Once, she redesigned a fragmented edge computing architecture into a unified pipeline, reducing latency by 30% and boosting ad-serving accuracy. She thrives in ambiguity, often mentoring junior engineers with dry wit and a refusal to accept “good enough.”  

Opal’s work ethic is a given. She’ll stay late to refactor legacy code or prototype a new sensor integration, always prioritizing reliability over speed. If you need someone who treats hardware as a puzzle to solve, not a barrier, she’s your person.
